steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Remember: Every point you make needs evidence. "Show, don't just tell." A quotation shows exactly what the writer did. | Technique: Introduce the quotation with your own words, then quote only the key words. The quotation becomes part of YOUR sentence. | Recommended: 5-8 key quotations per major text. Choose quotations that can be used for multiple themes or characters. Quality over quantity. | Top Tip: In closed-book exams, quotation recall under time pressure is critical. Spend the first 5 minutes of planning time jotting down the 3-4 quotations you will use. This prevents you forgetting key quotes mid-essay and ensures every paragraph has evidence ready before you start writing.
